comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official 2026-2027 prospectus API reconstructs the full-time 180-EC Dutch-taught curriculum. The 60-EC first year and 30-EC second-year common core are compulsory. The normalized target does not name one of the four Dutch graduation specialisations, so Ethics and Political Philosophy is selected by the documented official-order tie break. For that route, Normative Ethics and Global Justice form the 20-EC second-year thematic selection; Advanced Moral and Political Philosophy plus Naming and Necessity form a valid 10-EC core-course selection; and Virtue Ethics and Continental Political Philosophy form the 20-EC spring thematic selection. These are the first two spring options in the official Ethics and Political Philosophy group. The autumn semester holds the 30 EC elective space. The illustrated route completes 90 compulsory EC including Ethics, Philosophical Skills and Political Philosophy before its specialisation study. A 10-EC spring thesis and 30 EC of genuine elective space complete the degree. The part-time programme is officially described as content-identical but paced over 4.5 years, so the full-time curriculum is the neutral normalized structure.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target specifies the Dutch Philosophy bachelor but no graduation specialisation. The current official curriculum offers four equally formal Dutch routes and identifies no unspecialised completion route. Ethics and Political Philosophy is selected because it appears first in the current official curriculum, independently of UCR fit.

Ethics, moral judgment, justice, political and social philosophy
Knowledge, metaphysics, mind, language, reality and free will
Logic, critical argumentation, philosophical text analysis, writing and research methods
Comparative, global, cultural and technological philosophy and philosophical anthropology
Philosophy of science, scientific knowledge and objectivity

alternatives.label: Philosophy, Argument & Intellectual History
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines philosophical history, ethics, mind and free will with logic, politics, law, rhetoric, culture and humanities research.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines UCR’s dedicated philosophy courses with political thought, rhetoric, law, history, literature and cultural interpretation, covering the broadest defensible range of Leiden’s programme.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters from Fall 2026 through Spring 2029. Personal & Professional Development is in Year 1; all course offerings match the fixed cohort terms; none of the selected courses has an unmet formal prerequisite; and eight level-3 courses are concentrated in Years 2 and 3 after introductory philosophy, politics, rhetoric, history and interpretive work.

alternatives.label: Ethics, Politics, Justice & Institutions
alternatives.concept: A practical-philosophy route focused on moral judgment, justice, political institutions, law and social responsibility.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum forms a coherent normative sequence in ethics, political philosophy, justice, law, institutions, social movements and public reasoning.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces eleven courses in archaeology, literature, general history and rhetoric with comparative politics, criminal and constitutional law, EU law, modern and contemporary sociology, environmental justice, gender history and public policy analysis. The result prioritises normative public questions and institutions rather than broad philosophical and intellectual history.
progression: Law, Society & Justice is completed in semester 1 before the dependent law courses. All six terms retain four courses and the original selections; the offering repairs and formal prerequisites have been verified against the current workbook.

alternatives.label: Mind, Language, Knowledge & Science
alternatives.concept: A theoretical-philosophy route focused on mind, language, knowledge, reality and science, supported by cognitive science, psychology and AI.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum links philosophy of mind, logic and free will with cognition, psycholinguistics, empirical research, AI and machine learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces twelve courses in political philosophy, law, history, archaeology, literature and international politics with brain and behaviour, neurobiology, perception and action, psycholinguistics, social and experimental psychology, higher cognition, programming, machine learning, AI ethics and advanced research methods and statistics. Compared with the ethics route, it replaces law, institutions and social theory with sustained study of mind, language and science.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Introduction to Brain & Behavior in semester 1 precedes Psycholinguistics, which is offered in semester 2 for this cohort. The schedule includes seven 300-level courses.

blocks: Both introduce foundational Western philosophical traditions, including ancient thinkers; UCR is a broader historical survey.

Both study justification of moral judgments through major ethical theories, including consequentialist, Kantian and virtue traditions, using philosophical texts and arguments. Leiden also develops explicit metaethical distinctions.
Both introduce major political-philosophical concepts and arguments; UCR is thematic rather than a dedicated historical survey.
Both examine justice and rights beyond the state; UCR approaches the topic through human-rights law and philosophy.

The current Leiden course studies Islamic moral philosophy, self-cultivation and practical wisdom. The selected UCR courses offer related ethical reasoning but do not reproduce this specialised tradition.

Both critically read modern social thought about subjectivity, power, identity and social criticism. UCR Modern Sociology includes critical, phenomenological and decolonial perspectives; it is a partial social-theory relationship, not the full philosophical canon.

Both examine critical social theory and political agency in historically shaped social relations. UCR centres civil society, hegemony, solidarity and public spheres; Leiden centres dialectical materialism and Marxist/phenomenological political philosophy. The relationship is partial.
Mind, language, knowledge and human nature
Philosophy of Mind addresses knowledge, representation and mental states, covering part of Leiden’s broader epistemology component.
Both examine selfhood, time, agency and free will as metaphysical questions; UCR is a focused advanced seminar.
Both develop formal reasoning and validity; UCR combines logic with discrete mathematics and computing applications.
Both develop argument analysis, academic reasoning, writing, oral communication and critical engagement with claims.

UCR Ethics includes normative theories but is placed with the stronger foundational Ethics relationship. Its credits are not counted a second time against this advanced study of principles and their criticism.
The selected UCR courses do not directly cover this Leiden component’s specific philosophical subject or educational function; it remains a visible curricular difference.

General modern history does not directly teach the philosophical arguments and texts of this history-of-philosophy component.

General historical or policy research is not a sufficient subject-specific counterpart to the required independent philosophy thesis. Optional independent research is shown separately from the scheduled curriculum.
Literary close reading and a cross-period canon do not establish study of medieval philosophical doctrines or arguments.
International-relations explanatory theories do not adequately represent this specialist normative political-philosophy component.
Stylistic analysis of literary meaning is distinct from the analytic philosophical questions of naming, reference and necessity.
Primary-school rhetorical instruction and public-speaking practice are distinct from advanced moral and political philosophy.
Literary theories of meaning and interpretation do not reproduce the specific modern philosophical sequence.
Qualitative data-collection and analysis skills do not by themselves constitute philosophy of science or philosophical inquiry into scientific knowledge.

Leiden traces culture and Bildung through primary philosophical texts and critiques of cultural ideals. Emotion, literary interpretation and historical context are related but do not establish this primary philosophical subject.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match owns the general questions, historical breadth, argumentation and research interests. Two further generator-backed directions are coherent, feasible and materially distinct: ethics, politics and justice; and mind, language, knowledge and science. Their schedules differ pairwise by eleven to sixteen courses and all satisfy the hard constraints, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: Leiden combines 150 EC of philosophy study, including a required thesis, with 30 EC of elective space. It provides substantially more specialist work in philosophical history, knowledge, science, language and advanced research. The UCR alternatives share five dedicated Philosophy courses, with additional philosophical contributions from political thought, rights or AI ethics and specific complements from other disciplines. These are qualified interdisciplinary pathways, not the same Philosophy degree or a guarantee of credit transfer or master’s admission.

audience.programmeDescription: Philosophy at Leiden examines fundamental questions about knowledge, reality, values, culture and human life through philosophical texts and arguments. Its historical and systematic foundations lead to a specialisation and an independent philosophy thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: All three UCR pathways share introductory philosophy, ethics, philosophy of mind, philosophy of emotion and free will. The first adds intellectual and cultural history, argument and interpretation. The second develops ethics and public questions through politics, law and social theory. The third connects philosophical questions about mind and knowledge with cognition, language, research methods and AI. Leiden offers a much denser specialist philosophy sequence; empirical research, rhetoric and cultural study contribute different kinds of work.

curriculum.routeLabel: Dutch Philosophy programme; Ethics and Political Philosophy specialisation
curriculum.limitation: The illustrated 180 EC includes 30 EC of elective space and a 10 EC thesis with its compulsory seminar. The selected third-year courses, Virtue Ethics and Continental Political Philosophy, are examples within the specialisation. The illustration follows the current annual requirements and does not guarantee future course offerings. Entry and participation requirements apply. UCR compositions do not confer Leiden’s degree or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

cellNotes.text: UCR Ethics also covers normative theories. It is placed with foundational Ethics and counted only once.
Modern Sociology provides a partial relationship through critical social theory, phenomenology, power and identity; it does not cover the full continental-philosophy sequence.
UCR’s civil-society theory connects critical thought to collective life and political agency. Leiden studies a more specific Marxist and phenomenological tradition.
Philosophy of Mind contributes questions about self-knowledge, experience and representation. Leiden’s epistemology also addresses justification, truth, induction and scepticism.
Rhetoric develops argument analysis and communication. Leiden’s course specifically trains philosophical textual analysis and the writing of an original philosophy essay.
